The test image shows a corn leaf with a single large, elongated (cigar/canoe-shaped) tan-gray lesion. This is characteristic of a leaf disease. My top candidates from the leaf class list: Northern_Leaf_Blight, Gray_Leaf_Spot, Goss_S_Wilt, Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight, Anthracnose, Stewart_S_Disease, Eyespot, Carbonum_Leaf_Spot.

Let me view one reference from each top candidate.
NLB reference shows cigar-shaped tan lesions very similar to the test image. Let me check other candidates.
Gray Leaf Spot shows narrow, rectangular lesions bounded by veins - very different from the test image's broad cigar-shaped lesion. Not a match.
Goss's Wilt shows large water-soaked lesions with wavy edges and freckles - very different pattern. Not a match.
SCLB shows smaller, rectangular lesions bounded by veins - not matching the test image's large cigar-shaped lesion.
Anthracnose shows smaller lesions with dark brown/purple margins along the leaf edge - different from the test image's large central cigar-shaped lesion.
Stewart's Disease shows long bleached streaks along the leaf - different pattern from the discrete cigar-shaped lesion in the test image.

Eyespot shows many small circular spots with halos - completely different from the test image. Not a match.

Now let me use my last view on a second NLB reference to confirm the match.

Carbonum Leaf Spot shows many small circular spots - completely different from the test image.

All 8 reference views used. The test image clearly matches Northern Leaf Blight: the single large, elongated cigar/canoe-shaped tan-gray lesion is the hallmark symptom. No other candidate came close visually.
